problem: Outdoor VLN (Touchdown) is limited by scarce training data and by a single Manhattan environment. Learned speaker models and action predictors fail to generate good instructions and actions for out-of-domain driving videos.
motivation: Human-annotated VLN data is costly, and the existing augmentation methods (speakers, style transfer) are mostly indoor and add no new environments or temporal information. Large driving video datasets offer diverse cities and temporal dynamics, but they have no instructions or heading labels, so they need a robust and cheap way to be turned into VLN-style data.
key_idea: Turn caption-less BDD100K driving videos into VLN pre-training data by filling Touchdown-derived instruction templates with detected objects and actions predicted by an image-rotation-similarity turn predictor, then pre-train with MLM, ITM and NAP and transfer the instruction representation to the ORAR navigator.
insight: Simple classical components beat learned ones under a large domain gap. Replacing the template-infilling speaker with a learned LSTM speaker drops val TC from 34.5 to 27.1, removing GPT-2 template filtering drops it to 31.6, and swapping the rotation-based action predictor for a learned one drops it to 31.3. The learned turn predictor predicts almost all 'forward' on videos, while the rotation predictor gets 33% of turns in the human evaluation, versus 0% for the learned one. Gains come from richer visual and temporal data, not just more in-domain pairs, and the effect on unseen environments is smaller and noisier.
method: Template extraction: chunk Touchdown instructions with an LSTM-CRF, mask noun phrases as <OBJECT>, keep templates with one object and one direction word, and split them into turn/forward/stop types. GPT-2 loss filters out half the templates, leaving 3,004 turn, 269 forward and 92 stop templates.

Rotation-similarity action predictor: rotate frame t+1 left and right, compute windowed MSE against frame t, and read off left, forward or right from which window and rotation gives the best match. It needs no training (window 80°, shift 60°).
Object detection: a Mask-RCNN pre-trained on LVIS (Detectron2) detects objects, with frequent or unhelpful classes (bus, car, wheel, etc.) filtered out.

Instruction generation: sample BDD100K frames at 1 s, use trajectory lengths of 25–40, and merge consecutive forward actions (max 6) and consecutive turns. Generate one templated sentence per merged action and concatenate them. Manh50 gets the same templates, with actions taken from graph heading changes.

Stage 1 pre-training: VLN-Transformer (BERT + ResNet, cross-modal transformer) is trained on Touchdown, Manh50 and 6K BDD100K videos with MLM, ITM (4 negatives, including shuffled-viewpoint ones) and NAP, with equal loss weights, for 200k iterations at batch size 64.

Stage 2 fine-tuning: the contextual instruction representation from the pre-trained transformer is used as the input word embedding of the LSTM ORAR agent, which is fine-tuned on Touchdown with imitation learning (300 epochs).

setting.backbone: VLN-Transformer (BERT + ResNet, pre-trained) feeding an ORAR LSTM navigator (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: Touchdown (6,526 train), Manh50 (31k StreetLearn trajectories, synthetic instructions) and 6K BDD100K driving videos with template-generated instructions and predicted actions
setting.observation: Street View panoramas (Touchdown), with heading-centered views; egocentric video frames for pre-training
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph actions: forward, left, right, stop

numbers_note: Touchdown is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is given as 'Touchdown'; the paper's split is named 'Validation Set' and 'Test Set', mapped to val and test. Metrics are TC/SPD/SED. Table 1 gives the ORAR-BERT baseline at 30.6/30 TC, and PM-VLN (which uses GT path traces) at 33.0/33.4 TC.
results: VLN-Video reaches TC 34.5 on val and 31.7 on test, a new state of the art among agents without ground-truth path traces. It beats ORAR-BERT (30.6 / 30.0) by 3.9 and 1.7 TC, and ORAR (30.1 / 29.6) by 4.4 and 2.1 TC. PM-VLN, which sees GT path traces, is higher on test TC (33.4), but VLN-Video has much better SPD (11.2 vs 23.8).
limitations: Gains on test are small (about 1.7 TC over ORAR-BERT), and on unseen-environment splits gains are inconsistent, with test-unseen TC improving by only about 0.6 over ORAR-BERT.
Evaluated only on Touchdown with one pre-training/fine-tuning pairing (VLN-Transformer to ORAR), using a 6K-video subset of BDD100K.
Template-generated instructions are limited in diversity, and the rotation predictor is a heuristic that is only moderately accurate (33% of turns correct in the human study, on 50 samples).
